content:
When Apple launched the Apple Watch Series 12, two features stood out the most: the all-new Siri reporting capability, and the significantly improved heart rate monitor. Although these two features were among the reasons I decided to buy the new Apple Watch, I discovered there was much more that surprised me.

Battery and Charging

Although Apple's official website does not list any additional battery life improvement for the Apple Watch Series 12 over the Series 11, the battery does feel like it lasts longer. As I have written before, I was using WHOOP before the Apple Watch Series 12, and although I kept my Apple Watch, I never used it to track sleep.

After the launch event, I decided to try using the Apple Watch to track sleep. That said, on my Series 11, juggling both sleep tracking and charging was genuinely a bit of a hassle. After a day of use, I'd have to top it up a bit before bed, and then charge it again after waking up.

But the Series 12 does not have this problem. It has enough battery to last through the whole day and night, so now I just charge it after I wake up. The Apple Watch Series 12 also charges much faster, making the wait far less painful. According to Apple, 15 minutes of charging gets you 12 hours of use.

I suspect the all-new S11 chip (derived from the A20 Pro's 2nm design) is one of the main reasons the battery feels longer-lasting. Whatever the reason, being able to use the Apple Watch Series 12's sleep tracking without worrying about charging feels genuinely great. Another big advantage of the S11 chip? The Apple Watch Series 12 feels significantly faster, especially when using Siri.

Exclusive Software Features

The Series 12 finally adds a proper step counter as a watch face complication, which I love watching in the Smart Stack. Will this feature trickle down to older Apple Watches? Most likely. Apple has always counted steps before; the Series 12 just does it more accurately. Since the data is already there, I think Apple should have added this complication straight away. Regardless, having it on the Series 12 is still a good thing.

Another nice new feature is the entire Readiness app, which tells you how you're doing today based on last night's sleep, yesterday's activity, and your vital signs. This is similar to WHOOP's recovery score, and I'm certainly thrilled to see Apple bringing this feature to the Apple Watch. Unfortunately, it's limited to the Series 12, but considering Apple doesn't want to use less accurate data for its calculations, I can understand why.

Summary

Overall, the Apple Watch Series 12 is a pretty solid upgrade. Although it's an S-year refresh, if you care about whether your Apple Watch actually gains functionality rather than just a cosmetic change, I'd say this might be the biggest year-on-year upgrade since the Apple Watch Series 4.

The case is indeed slightly thicker compared to the Series 10 and 11. I use a black background watch face, so I don't really notice it — though I hope Apple can improve on this in the next generation.

Another point worth mentioning: the aluminium case of the Apple Watch Series 12 uses Ceramic Shield 2, offering significantly better scratch resistance than older Apple Watch models. I haven't had mine long enough to truly put this to the test, but so far the Apple Watch remains completely unscathed.

  • MOFT MagSafe snap-on phone stand wallet (for iPhone)
